papers.title: Future-Information Leakage in 30-Day Readmission Prediction: An Empirical Audit and a Calibrated Electronic Health Record Model in Medicare-Insured Adults
papers.summary:
-  We classified 1088 files: 375 data, 465 code, 26 documentation, 213 materials, 2 output, 7 unknown.
-  We found 12 tabular data files and extracted 492 columns from 10 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 4 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  2 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (results/table1_cohort.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; thiagobandeira1/Medicare-30day-Readmission-MIMIC-IV-v16.1-jamia.zip/thiagobandeira1-Medicare-30day-Readmission-MIMIC-IV-f1f90fa/results/table1_cohort.csv: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: results/table1_cohort.csv, thiagobandeira1/Medicare-30day-Readmission-MIMIC-IV-v16.1-jamia.zip/thiagobandeira1-Medicare-30day-Readmission-MIMIC-IV-f1f90fa/results/table1_cohort.csv. We ran automated data-quality checks on 492 columns; 6 columns have at least one potential issue (4 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 2 columns with numeric values stored as text). We detected demographic column for Race.

papers.summary:
-  We classified 10690 files: 8449 data, 339 code, 1374 documentation, 144 materials, 1 output, 383 unknown.
-  We found 124 tabular data files and extracted 2296 columns from 117 of them.

papers.title: Assessing the Accuracy of the NeuroBooster Array for GBA1 Variant Detection
papers.summary:
-  We classified 10 files: 2 data, 2 code, 6 documentation.
-  We found 2 tabular data files and extracted 25 columns from 2 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 25 columns; 14 columns have at least one potential issue (8 columns whose name suggests personal information; 4 columns with inconsistent category casing; 4 columns whose values look like personal information; 2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long). 2 of 2 spreadsheet files have at least one formatting issue (colour coding, merged cells, empty rows/columns, or an offset header).

papers.title: Accounting for Insulin-on-board in Large Language Model Advice about Pediatric Hyperglycemia
papers.summary:
-  We classified 34 files: 19 data, 13 code, 2 documentation.
-  We found 5 tabular data files and extracted 31 columns from 5 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 1 study group (ex1), plus 2 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata). We ran automated data-quality checks on 31 columns; 11 columns have at least one potential issue (10 columns of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long).

papers.title: A Global Atlas of Immune Alleles Reveals Health-Relevant Variation Across Groups
papers.summary:
-  We classified 134 files: 107 data, 13 code, 6 documentation, 3 materials, 5 unknown.
-  We found 96 tabular data files and extracted 637 columns from 90 of them.
-  We grouped the files into 3 study groups (ex1, ex2, ex3), plus 5 collection-level files (README/ro-crate metadata).
-  1 tabular data file could not be read because it was not downloaded. This can happen for private repositories or failed downloads; you can also pass `local_path` to point at a local copy.
-  5 files read as a table but are not a usable rectangular dataset (Table_S1.txt: 75% of columns are free text, not variables; Table_S8.txt: 80% of columns are free text, not variables; Table_S9.txt: 88% of columns are free text, not variables; input.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables; input_fastq.txt: 100% of columns are free text, not variables). No columns were extracted and they were not sent to the LLM. Share the underlying data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable) with a codebook: Table_S1.txt, Table_S8.txt, Table_S9.txt, input.txt, input_fastq.txt. We ran automated data-quality checks on 637 columns; 69 columns have at least one potential issue (35 columns with numeric values stored as text; 30 columns with no observed values (entirely empty); 2 columns whose name contains file-illegal characters or is excessively long; 1 column of free text that may contain personal detail; 1 column whose name suggests personal information).
